desk.name: halloween
desk.notes: All five examples are genuinely Halloween shorts and the calendar/event call is right (3 days to 2026-10-31, "one piece, not a series"). But "halloween" is a holiday, not a mechanism: the evidence holds real sub-formats (costume ranking "Part N" by 2 creators, pet costume, SFX-makeup fail, costume ideas) that the card never names, and the production approach ("original music or parody track") comes from the mislabelled Music cluster and matches none of the five videos. Three of five examples are 1.1M–14M-subscriber channels (not shown). The three briefs are fixed templates: "Music-led examples" is false (0/5 music videos; one hook flag triggered it) and "mostly episodic part N" rests on 1/5; six of eight production steps are identical across briefs; TikTok Creator Rewards (≥1 min) is listed against a 21–39 s target.

desk.name: Avengers Doomsday
desk.notes: A trailer-release event, correctly typed and correctly held at "monitor". But 2 of the 4 "verified examples" are the studio's own promo (IndiaMarvel, Hindi + English cuts of the same Special Look), so "3 independent creators" counts Marvel as a creator; 0 qualified; the other two are 16-min reaction videos in German and Indonesian. Card says "11 independent creators so far" in timing and 3 in facts; "short-form examples (median 954s)"; category "Animation & Art" is a lossy mapping of YouTube's "Film & Animation" for a live-action trailer and is what makes this the highest "fit" (68) on the desk. No IP/derivative-risk note for a Marvel property. nextCheck asks for "two or more other creators publishing their own version" although two independent reaction videos are already in the evidence.

desk.name: 생기는 일
desk.notes: "X하면 생기는 일" ("what happens when X") is a generic Korean title template spanning a Tokyo liver-dish video, a dating TOP5 and two cat/dog videos — a title fragment, not a meme; the desk has a "title fragment" exclusion that this should have hit. Category "Food & Cooking" fits 1 of 4. Counts are honest (2 qualified + 2 mid-size, 3 extra videos by one creator excluded) and "monitor" with "examples in English or Spanish" is the right call, but the item is 100% Korean and offers the owner nothing. Monetization suitability 82 (highest on the desk) sits next to fit 35 with no explanation.

desk.name: 아이폰 듀오
desk.notes: Coherent topic (iPhone Duo breakage/display-defect controversy, Samsung's reply ad) but it is product news: the cluster contains KBS News and MTN clips, yet isNewsEvent=false and the type is "meme" at 85%. "Emerging" reflects the radar first seeing the cluster 8h ago; the videos are 48–68h old, the largest is at 0.3× its lifetime average and the trend-level coolingShare is 1.0. Timing says "5 independent creators so far", facts say 3. Category "Entertainment" instead of Tech. Should have been excluded as a news event.

desk.name: Upin Ipin
desk.notes: Two of the three "independent creators" are the brand's own Malay and Indonesian channels uploading the same 18-minute episode (Ketam Nipah / Kepiting Nipah); the third is a 13 s behind-the-scenes short. A studio's episode schedule for a copyrighted children's IP is not a creator opportunity. "Emerging" for 6.4-day-old videos with 0 new creators in 48h is wrong. production.feasibleIn2h=false (1.5–4h) on a ≤2h desk; language "latin" (Malay/Indonesian undetected); eligibility lines are Shorts/TikTok boilerplate on a long-form item; no IP note.

lane.notes: Counts are pool-level and arithmetically honest (e.g. comedy 342 creators / 459 videos / 308 qualified) but mix every language. Examples are mostly on-pool, with junk: two 4–6 s "Talking Tom" app clips in animal comedy, a Shopee commercial and label MVs as "music videos", a fashion-runway clip (Heemi) and an 18.8K-view rejected video as "AI-generated video". Sub-formats are a mix of junk and the best signal in the whole snapshot: "karwachauth" is a festival (calendar) not a structure, "mbappe" and "haaland" are the same 3D football-star parody format split in two (6 creators, 63M/15M/12M/9.8M/8M/4.6M/4.1M/3.2M views, English, 13–31 s, small channels), "tf2" (SFM meme animations, 6 creators) and "visualizer" are real. The AI couple POV storytime channels (Nyx and Ollie 27.7M/14.7M, Lila and Felix 53.8M) sit in the storytime pool with "no shared structure" although they share the #pov #foryou #storytime #fyp stack. Useful because it is the only place the owner-fit opportunities appear; not useful as designed: bare keywords, no action, "did not clear the desk gate (see the excluded reasons)" with no per-pool reason.

strengths: Every desk and feed claim is traceable: verified platform statistics, URLs, ages, measured velocity windows (hours stated), lifetime-vs-measured ratios; headline counts (creators / videos / qualified / "N other cluster videos not counted") match the examples shown.

Honest hedging: "provisional" growth, "history Nh; measurements need 24h", "visual style not inspected", mid-size successes separated from qualified hits, dominance cautions ("56% of views is one video").

The exclusion funnel is strict and mostly right: 310 of 316 clusters rejected with stated reasons; the "uncertain" bucket agrees 10/10; news, streams, fragments and generic tags are kept off the desk; nothing is padded (5 items, 1 actionable).
Monitored items state what would change the verdict (nextCheck) — the right decision-support pattern even when the item itself is weak.
Calendar handling is correct and useful: countdown to the date, "attention collapses after the date", "one original piece, not a series".

The lane's sub-format extraction finds real structures the clustering misses (3D football-star parody, TF2 SFM memes, visualizers), and the Viral Now cards' numbers are internally consistent (floors, percentiles, measured vs lifetime).
weaknesses: The desk gives an English/Spanish AI-animation creator nothing to make today except "Halloween is in 3 days": 4 of 5 items are Korean, Malay or Hindi-language topics with zero EN/ES examples, and three of them are news, a studio trailer and a children's-TV brand — not formats.

The best opportunity in the snapshot — 3D football-star parody shorts (SWIFT X RELOAD 63M, oddlyokay 15M + 9.8M, Mischief Time 12M, H4X 8M, BG5B 4.6M, ainimal-rescue-ai 4.1M + 3.2M; English, 13–31 s, three of six creators on channels under 40K subscribers, two new ≥3M hits in the last 27h) — is invisible on the desk and appears only as the lane keywords "mbappe"/"haaland", because the sub-format promotion treats each video's post-peak slowdown as the format cooling.

Timing labels are artefacts of the radar's own age: all 5,113 records were first seen on 2026-10-28 and every cluster "first seen 1–9h ago", so "emerging" is applied to 6-day-old episodes and 2–3-day-old news; trend-level coolingShare is ≥0.8 for most real formats, which is why the "cooling → skip" gate leaves only calendar events and freshly detected foreign clusters.

Type classification fails outside the "uncertain" bucket: 58% agreement overall, 0/2 on memes (both wrong: a news story and a title fragment), 3/9 on formats (a calendar day at 95%, a 77%-one-video cluster at 90%, subjects as formats); brand/studio channels count as independent creators (Marvel India, two Upin & Ipin channels).

The three briefs are fixed templates with the name substituted (always Character-led; Levels or Reversal; Song, Explainer or Mashup by a single hook flag): for Halloween "Music-led examples" is false (0 of 5), "mostly episodic part N" rests on 1 of 5, six of eight steps repeat verbatim, and TikTok Creator Rewards (≥1 min) is listed against a 21–39 s target.

Early Radar: half of the top 10 are below their own lifetime average (velocityRatio 0.69–0.93) with percentile ranks of "top 36–59%", carried by a noisy acceleration ratio; the list includes a broadcaster promo (JioHotstar) and two kids-autoplay compilations; 19 of 40 entries have velocityRatio < 1.

Classifier errors visible from titles alone: "GOAT" → Animals & Pets, an AI POV storytime short → Music, Film & Animation → "Animation & Art" (makes a live-action Marvel trailer the top "fit"), French → "latin"/"en", Malay/Indonesian → "latin", a Hindi title → "en".

Monetization is boilerplate: Instagram Reels has no general ad-revenue share; Shorts/TikTok eligibility lines are pasted onto an 18-minute long-form item; no IP/Content-ID risk line for Marvel or Upin & Ipin; "suitability 82" for a Korean title trope next to fit 35 is unexplained.

Card inconsistencies: "11 independent creators so far" (timing) vs 3 (facts) on Avengers, 5 vs 3 on 아이폰 듀오; "short-form examples (median 954s)"; channel size never shown although 3 of 5 Halloween examples are 1.1M–14M-subscriber channels; 316 considered vs 315 accounted (one item apparently dropped by the per-category cap, the only silent path in desk.ts, without a logged reason); a 72-minute DAZN broadcast stream sits at rank 13 of a feed that says streams are excluded.
fixes: 1. Promote lane sub-formats to the desk and measure format freshness by the flow of new independent hits (e.g. ≥2 qualified examples younger than 72h from different channels) instead of per-video velocityRatio; a short-form, EN/ES sub-format with ≥4 creators and ≥2 qualified hits should reach "research" or "create today" (the 3D football parody would have been the top item today). Merge sub-formats whose examples overlap (mbappe/haaland).

2. Fix the type and independence rules: any broadcaster/news channel in the clean set → event+news (exclude); channels sharing an owner/brand or a studio's promo → one creator and an "IP-owned entity: derivative risk" flag (Marvel, Upin & Ipin); phrase clusters whose examples span unrelated subjects → fragment (생기는 일); calendar names → event even when adoption is wide (Black Cat).

3. Base timing on content, not on the radar's clock: "emerging" only when the clean examples are young and new creators appeared in 48h; show acceleration vs the previous interval beside the lifetime ratio; require velocityRatio ≥ 1 or an age-percentile ≤ 25% for Early Radar; exclude broadcaster promos, kids compilations (>10 min, 0 comments) and stream recordings from both feeds.

4. Generate briefs from the observed sub-mechanisms (costume ranking "Part N", pet costume, SFX fail) rather than fixed character/levels/song templates; claim a hook ("music-led", "mostly episodic") only when ≥50% of clean examples carry it; de-duplicate steps; make the TikTok ≥1 min line conditional on the suggested duration and add an IP-risk line when the entity is a brand.

5. Clean the cards: one creator count per card, fix "short-form (median 954s)", show subscriber counts and EN/ES share on evidence, print the per-pool exclusion reason in the lane, log the per-category-cap drop in excluded, and fix the keyword category mapping (GOAT, Film & Animation → Animation & Art) and language detection (fr/ms/id).
